cards.back: Tuve un dolor de cabeza horrible
cards.translation: Very common health-related chunk.

cards.back: No pude entender lo que pasó

cards.front: I put too many expectations on myself
cards.translation: Very useful emotional self-reflection chunk.

cards.front: I came to Spain to start over

cards.translation: Strong emotional life-story structure.

cards.front: I brought up the topic during dinner

cards.back: De repente me sentí mucho mejor

cards.front: I spent the whole weekend studying

entender in indefinido = moment of comprehension.

cards.example: Tenía demasiadas cosas en la cabeza.
cards.translation: Very common accidental structure in Spanish.
sentir in indefinido = specific emotional reaction.

cards.front: I decided to take a break

cards.front: I finally managed to finish it
cards.translation: conseguir = to manage/achieve successfully.

cards.example: Tenía demasiadas cosas en la cabeza.

cards.back: De repente me acordé de algo importante

cards.front: I kept thinking about it all day

cards.front: I ended up liking Madrid a lot
cards.translation: acabar + gerund = to end up doing something.

cards.front: I helped a friend with his project

cards.example: Para no ir con prisas hoy.

cards.front: I prepared for the interview all week

cards.front: I reviewed the document several times

cards.front: I took advantage of the free time

cards.translation: aprovechar = to make good use of.

cards.front: I improved a lot this month
cards.translation: mejorar = improve.

cards.front: I supported my wife during a difficult period
cards.back: Apoyé a mi mujer durante una etapa difícil
cards.example: Y ella hizo lo mismo conmigo.
cards.translation: apoyar = emotional/social support verb.

cards.back: Discutimos otra vez sobre el trabajo
cards.translation: discutir = to argue/discuss intensely.

cards.front: I relaxed a bit this weekend
cards.back: Me relajé un poco este fin de semana
cards.translation: relajarse = emotional recovery verb.

cards.front: I got excited about the opportunity
cards.translation: ilusionarse = to become excited/hopeful.

cards.front: I realized what the real problem was
cards.back: Me di cuenta de cuál era el verdadero problema
cards.example: Y todo empezó a tener sentido.
cards.translation: darse cuenta de = to realize.

cards.front: The situation turned out better than expected
cards.back: La situación resultó mejor de lo esperado
cards.example: Y me quedé mucho más tranquilo.
cards.translation: resultar = to turn out/result.
parecer = to seem/appear.

cards.front: I gradually got used to the rhythm
cards.back: Poco a poco me acostumbré al ritmo
cards.translation: acostumbrarse a = to get used to.

cards.front: I continued learning even when I was tired
cards.back: Seguí aprendiendo incluso cuando estaba cansado
cards.translation: seguir + gerund/continuation structure.

cards.front: I changed many habits this year
cards.translation: Natural self-improvement context.

cards.front: I tried to explain it clearly
cards.translation: Very useful work communication chunk.

cards.front: I managed to disconnect for a while
cards.translation: desconectar = mentally disconnect/unwind.

cards.front: I started taking things more calmly
cards.back: Empecé a tomarme las cosas con más calma
cards.translation: tomarse las cosas con calma = important emotional chunk.

cards.front: I ended up understanding his point
cards.back: Acabé entendiendo su punto de vista
cards.example: Aunque al principio no estaba de acuerdo.
cards.translation: acabar + gerund = eventual realization.

cards.front: I avoided checking my phone constantly
cards.translation: Very modern daily-life chunk.
con antelación = beforehand/in advance.

cards.front: I reviewed my notes before the meeting
cards.back: Revisé mis apuntes antes de la reunión
cards.translation: apuntes = notes.

cards.front: I fixed things with my friend
cards.back: Arreglé las cosas con mi amigo
cards.example: Y ahora estamos bien otra vez.
cards.translation: arreglar las cosas = repair a relationship/problem.

cards.front: Things got worse after the meeting
cards.back: Las cosas empeoraron después de la reunión
cards.example: Había mucha tensión en el equipo.

cards.front: I relaxed after hearing the news

cards.translation: Very common natural Spanish closure phrase.

cards.front: I was thinking about changing jobs
cards.front example: When suddenly another company called me.
cards.back: Estaba pensando en cambiar de trabajo
cards.example: Cuando de repente me llamaron de otra empresa.
cards.translation: Imperfecto gives the background action; indefinido introduces the event that interrupts it. pensar en = to think about.

cards.front: I was having dinner when he called me
cards.front example: I wasn't expecting the call at all.
cards.example: No me esperaba la llamada para nada.
cards.translation: Estaba cenando = ongoing background; me llamó = completed interrupting event.

cards.front: I didn't understand what was happening
cards.front example: Everything happened very quickly.
cards.translation: Imperfecto describes the ongoing state of not understanding; ocurrió marks the completed event.

cards.front: I was feeling a bit strange that day
cards.front example: I didn't really know why.
cards.back: Ese día me sentía un poco raro
cards.translation: Sentirse in imperfecto describes an ongoing emotional state.

cards.front: I thought everything was going well
cards.front example: But then I received some unexpected news.
cards.example: Pero luego recibí una noticia inesperada.
cards.translation: Pensaba + iba = two imperfectos describing a past belief and the background situation.

cards.front: I was about to leave when she arrived
cards.front example: So I stayed a little longer.
cards.back: Estaba a punto de irme cuando llegó
cards.example: Así que me quedé un rato más.
cards.translation: Estar a punto de + infinitive = to be about to do something.

cards.front: I used to work from home
cards.front example: And I had quite a lot of flexibility.
cards.translation: Imperfecto expresses a repeated or habitual past situation.

cards.front: I used to go there every Friday
cards.front example: But I haven't been there for months.
cards.example: Pero hace meses que no voy.
cards.translation: Ir → iba. Imperfecto is natural with repeated past habits.

cards.front: I didn't use to understand this
cards.front example: Now it seems much clearer to me.
cards.example: Ahora me resulta mucho más claro.
cards.translation: Antes + imperfecto describes a past state that has changed.

cards.front: I was trying to explain the situation
cards.front example: But nobody seemed to be listening to me.
cards.translation: Estaba intentando = ongoing attempt. intentar + infinitive = to try to do something.

cards.front example: So I had to explain it again.
cards.example: Así que tuve que explicarlo otra vez.
cards.translation: Parecer = to seem. Tuve que = I had to, a completed past obligation.

cards.front: I didn't know what to say
cards.front example: My mind went completely blank.
cards.translation: Saber → sabía. No sabía qué decir is a very common conversational pattern.

cards.front: I was worried about what might happen
cards.front example: But I tried not to think about it too much.
cards.back: Me preocupaba lo que pudiera pasar
cards.example: Pero intenté no darle demasiadas vueltas.
cards.translation: Preocuparse describes an ongoing concern. darle vueltas a algo = to overthink something.

cards.front: I kept telling myself that everything would be fine
cards.front example: Even though I was quite nervous inside.
cards.back: Me repetía que todo saldría bien
cards.example: Aunque por dentro estaba bastante nervioso.
cards.translation: Me repetía = repeated background action. Saldría = conditional for future viewed from a past perspective.

cards.front: I didn't expect it to happen so quickly
cards.front example: It completely caught me by surprise.
cards.back: No esperaba que ocurriera tan rápido
cards.translation: No esperaba = imperfecto for an expectation at that time. ocurrir is imperfect subjunctive after esperaba que.

cards.front: I was getting used to the new routine
cards.front example: At first it was quite difficult for me.
cards.back: Me estaba acostumbrando a la nueva rutina
cards.translation: Estar + gerund expresses an ongoing process. acostumbrarse a = to get used to.

cards.front example: But little by little I adapted to the new situation.
cards.example: Pero poco a poco me fui adaptando.
cards.translation: Resultar = to seem/turn out. adaptarse = to adapt.

cards.front example: And little by little I regained my confidence.
cards.example: Y empecé a recuperar la confianza.
cards.translation: Ir + gerund emphasizes gradual progression. recuperar = to recover/regain.

cards.front: I didn't realize how tired I was
cards.front example: Until I got home.
cards.back: No me daba cuenta de lo cansado que estaba
cards.translation: Darse cuenta in imperfecto describes an ongoing lack of awareness; llegué marks the specific moment.

cards.front: When I arrived, everyone was already eating
cards.front example: So I sat down with them.
cards.back: Cuando llegué, todos ya estaban comiendo
cards.example: Así que me senté con ellos.
cards.translation: Llegué = completed event; estaban comiendo = ongoing background action.

cards.front: I wanted to leave, but I stayed
cards.front example: In the end, the conversation became interesting.
cards.example: Al final la conversación se puso interesante.
cards.translation: Quería = intention/background state; me quedé = completed decision/action.

cards.front: I felt more confident after that
cards.front example: And I started speaking more easily.
cards.back: Después de eso me sentí más seguro
cards.example: Y empecé a hablar con más soltura.
cards.translation: Sentirse in indefinido marks a change in emotional state. con soltura = fluently/naturally.

cards.front: I realized I was overthinking everything
cards.front example: And I decided to stop doing it so much.
cards.back: Me di cuenta de que estaba dándole demasiadas vueltas a todo
cards.translation: Me di cuenta = completed realization; estaba dándole vueltas = ongoing mental process.

cards.front: I was looking for a solution
cards.front example: When suddenly an idea came to me.
cards.example: Cuando se me ocurrió una idea.
cards.translation: Estaba buscando = background action. ocurrírsele algo a alguien = for an idea to occur to someone.

cards.front example: And everything started to make sense.
cards.back: De repente se me ocurrió una idea
cards.translation: Ocurrírsele algo a alguien = to suddenly think of/have an idea. encajar = to fit/make sense.

cards.front example: But reality was different.
cards.translation: Esperarse algo = to expect something. The reflexive form is very common in conversation.

cards.front: I didn't feel like going out
cards.front example: I preferred to stay at home.
cards.translation: Apetecer = to feel like/want to do something. Very useful Spain Spanish verb.

cards.front: I felt like having a coffee
cards.front example: So I went to a café.
cards.example: Así que fui a una cafetería.
cards.translation: Me apetecía = I felt like having. Apetecer is normally used with an indirect-object structure.

cards.front example: When it started raining.
cards.translation: Estaba disfrutando = ongoing action interrupted by empezó.

cards.front: We were having a great time
cards.front example: Until we had to leave.
cards.translation: Pasárselo genial = to have a great time. Very natural conversational Spanish.

cards.front: I was talking to a friend when I got the news
cards.front example: It really surprised me.
cards.back: Estaba hablando con un amigo cuando me enteré de la noticia
cards.translation: Estaba hablando = background; me enteré = completed discovery. enterarse de = to find out.

cards.front: I had been thinking about it for days
cards.front example: But I still hadn't made a decision.
cards.example: Pero todavía no había tomado una decisión.
cards.translation: Llevar + time + gerund = to have been doing something for a period of time.

cards.front: I was becoming more comfortable speaking Spanish
cards.front example: And that really encouraged me.
cards.back: Me estaba sintiendo más cómodo hablando español
cards.translation: Ongoing emotional development uses imperfecto/progressive structure. animar = encourage/cheer up.

cards.front: I was afraid of making a mistake
cards.front example: But every time I worried about it less.
cards.example: Pero cada vez me preocupaba menos.
cards.translation: Tener miedo de + infinitive = to be afraid of doing something.

cards.front: I didn't want to interrupt you
cards.front example: So I waited until you finished speaking.
cards.example: Por eso esperé a que terminaras.
cards.translation: Quería = imperfecto because it describes intention at that moment. esperar a que + subjunctive is required.

cards.front: I was wondering if you could help me
cards.front example: It's a fairly quick thing.
cards.translation: Me preguntaba = softens a request. podrías = conditional for politeness.

cards.front: I thought you were going to come
cards.front example: That's why I didn't message you.
cards.translation: Pensaba = past belief; ibas a venir = near/future-in-the-past construction.

cards.front: I was going to call you
cards.front example: But it got very late.
cards.translation: Ir a + infinitive in imperfecto expresses an intended future action from a past perspective. hacerse tarde = to get late.

cards.front: I was having a bad day
cards.front example: And everything was annoying me.
cards.translation: Imperfecto describes the ongoing state/background of the day. molestar = to bother/annoy.

cards.front: Everything was going according to plan
cards.front example: Until a problem came up.
cards.translation: Ir = to go/progress. surgir = to arise/come up.

cards.front: Then an unexpected problem came up
cards.front example: And we had to change our plans.
cards.example: Y tuvimos que cambiar de planes.
cards.translation: Surgir = to arise. Indefinido marks the new event in the story.

cards.front: We had to change our plans
cards.front example: But in the end everything went well.
cards.example: Pero al final salió todo bien.
cards.translation: Tuvimos que = completed past obligation. cambiar de planes = change plans.

cards.front: In the end, everything worked out
cards.front example: Although at first things looked pretty bad.
cards.example: Aunque al principio pintaba bastante mal.
cards.translation: Salir bien = to work out well. Pintar mal = to look bad/not look promising.

cards.front example: I no longer had to think about it so much.
cards.example: Ya no tenía que pensar tanto.
cards.translation: Parecía = background impression. parecer = to seem.

cards.front: Once I got the hang of it, it became easier
cards.front example: I no longer had to think about it so much.
cards.back: Cuando le cogí el tranquillo, se volvió más fácil
cards.example: Ya no tenía que pensar tanto.
cards.translation: Cogerle el tranquillo a algo = to get the hang of it. Very useful colloquial expression.

cards.front: I was slowly getting the hang of it
cards.front example: And every time it came out more naturally.
cards.back: Poco a poco le iba cogiendo el tranquillo
cards.example: Y cada vez me salía con más naturalidad.
cards.translation: Iba + gerund emphasizes gradual progress. salir con naturalidad = come out naturally.

cards.front: I felt like I was making progress
cards.front example: And that gave me quite a lot of motivation.
cards.example: Y eso me daba bastante motivación.
cards.translation: Sentía = ongoing perception; estaba avanzando = ongoing progress.

cards.front: I finally realized what I had been doing wrong
cards.front example: And since then I've tried to avoid it.
cards.back: Por fin me di cuenta de lo que estaba haciendo mal
cards.translation: Completed realization + imperfect progressive action. desde entonces = since then.

cards.front: I was making the same mistake over and over
cards.front example: Until someone pointed it out to me.
cards.back: Cometía el mismo error una y otra vez
cards.example: Hasta que alguien me lo señaló.
cards.translation: Imperfecto for repeated past behavior. señalar = to point something out.

cards.front example: Today I need to disconnect from everything for a while.
cards.translation: Future for a future intention. encargarse de = to take care of/deal with.

cards.front example: As soon as I have any news.
cards.translation: Avisar = to let someone know/inform someone. Very useful everyday verb.

cards.front example: If anything changes, I'll let you know.
cards.translation: Mantener al tanto = to keep someone informed. Natural professional/social phrase.

cards.front example: I'm very tired.
cards.back: Probablemente me quedaré en casa esta noche
cards.translation: Future expresses a prediction/intention. quedarse = to stay.

cards.front example: That's why he's not answering.
cards.translation: Future can express present probability: estará = he is probably.

cards.front example: It looks like it costs quite a lot.
cards.translation: Future probability is very common in Spanish for guesses about the present. tener pinta de = look/seem likely to.

cards.front example: Let me know when you're nearby.
cards.translation: Future for asking about a future event. cuando + future reference takes present subjunctive.

cards.front: I'll see what I can do
cards.front example: But I don't promise anything.
cards.translation: Veré = I will see. Useful when you cannot promise a result.

cards.front: I'll try to sort it out
cards.front example: And I'll tell you as soon as I know more.
cards.example: Y te cuento algo en cuanto sepa más.
cards.translation: Intentaré = future of intentar. solucionar = to solve/fix an issue.

cards.front example: I don't want to do it in a rush.
cards.translation: Future prediction + necesitar = to need. con prisas = in a rush.

cards.front: Could you give me a hand?
cards.front example: I only have one more thing left to finish.
cards.example: Solo me queda una cosa por terminar.
cards.translation: Conditional for polite requests. echar una mano = to give a hand/help.

cards.front: Would you mind waiting a moment?
cards.front example: I have to finish this first.
cards.translation: Te importaría = very polite conditional request. importar = to mind.

cards.front: I would like to ask you something
cards.front example: It's a slightly sensitive topic.
cards.example: Es un tema un poco delicado.
cards.translation: Me gustaría = I would like. Conditional gives politeness and softens the request.

cards.front example: I don't feel like going out today.
cards.translation: Preferiría = I would rather. Conditional expresses preference politely.

cards.front: I would probably do the same
cards.front example: I don't see many alternatives.
cards.translation: Conditional expresses a hypothetical reaction. alternativa = alternative.

cards.front: I wouldn't do that if I were you
cards.front example: But obviously it's your decision.
cards.back: Yo no haría eso si fuera tú
cards.translation: Classic hypothetical: conditional + imperfect subjunctive. fuera = imperfect subjunctive of ser.

cards.front: If I had more time, I'd travel more
cards.front example: But right now I don't have much time.
cards.back: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más
cards.example: Pero ahora mismo voy bastante justo.
cards.translation: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional = hypothetical present situation. ir justo de tiempo = have little time.

cards.front: If I could, I'd take a few days off
cards.front example: I need to disconnect from everything for a while.
cards.back: Si pudiera, me tomaría unos días libres
cards.translation: Pudiera = imperfect subjunctive; me tomaría = conditional. tomarse días libres = take days off.

cards.front: If I were you, I'd talk to her first
cards.front example: That way you could avoid misunderstandings.
cards.back: Si fuera tú, hablaría con ella primero
cards.translation: Standard advice structure: si fuera tú + conditional. malentendido = misunderstanding.

cards.front: I'd be happier if I had more free time
cards.front example: I've been extremely busy lately.
cards.back: Sería más feliz si tuviera más tiempo libre
cards.translation: Conditional expresses the hypothetical result; imperfect subjunctive expresses the hypothetical condition. ir a tope = be extremely busy.

cards.front: I would have done it differently
cards.front example: But at that time I didn't have all the information.
cards.back: Lo habría hecho de otra manera
cards.example: Pero en aquel momento no tenía toda la información.
cards.translation: Conditional perfect = habría + participle. Used for hypothetical actions in the past.

cards.front: I would have called you, but I didn't have your number
cards.front example: I remembered too late.
cards.back: Te habría llamado, pero no tenía tu número
cards.translation: Habría llamado = unrealized past action. Imperfecto describes the background reason.

cards.front example: There are several factors I hadn't considered.
cards.example: Hay algunos factores que no había considerado.
cards.translation: Debería = conditional of deber, often used for advice or soft self-recommendation. replanteárselo = reconsider it.

cards.front: You should give it another thought
cards.front example: You don't have to decide today.
cards.translation: Deberías = soft advice. pensárselo = to think something over.

cards.front: It would be better to wait
cards.front example: That way we'll have more information.
cards.translation: Sería mejor = it would be better. Conditional softens advice.

cards.front example: Worst case, they'll say no.
cards.example: Como mucho, te dirán que no.
cards.translation: No estaría de más = it wouldn't hurt / it wouldn't be a bad idea. Very useful idiomatic phrase.

cards.front example: We don't have enough time right now.
cards.example: Ahora mismo no tenemos tiempo suficiente.
cards.translation: Deberíamos = conditional advice. aplazar = postpone.

cards.front: I'd suggest talking to your manager
cards.front example: Maybe they can give you a hand.
cards.back: Yo sugeriría hablar con tu jefe
cards.translation: Sugeriría = conditional makes the suggestion less forceful. echar una mano = help.

cards.front: I'd avoid making a decision right now
cards.front example: I'd wait until I had more information.
cards.back: Yo evitaría tomar una decisión ahora mismo
cards.translation: Evitaría = I would avoid. Conditional expresses cautious advice.

cards.front: I'd take the opportunity if I were you
cards.front example: Opportunities like this don't come along very often.
cards.back: Yo aprovecharía la oportunidad si fuera tú
cards.translation: Aprovechar = make use of/take advantage of. Hypothetical advice structure.

cards.front: I might go if the weather improves
cards.front example: We'll see what happens tomorrow.
cards.back: Igual voy si mejora el tiempo
cards.translation: Igual + present can mean 'maybe/perhaps' in colloquial Spain Spanish.

cards.front example: It depends on how the afternoon goes.
cards.back: Igual me uno a vosotros más tarde
cards.example: Depende de cómo vaya la tarde.
cards.translation: Igual = maybe/perhaps in colloquial Spain. unirse = to join.

cards.front: I'll probably have finished by then
cards.front example: So we can meet without any problem.
cards.back: Para entonces probablemente ya habré terminado
cards.example: Así que podremos quedar sin problema.
cards.translation: Future perfect = habré + participle. Used for an action completed before a future point.

cards.front: By next month, I'll have finished the course
cards.front example: After that I want to start another one.
cards.back: Para el mes que viene habré terminado el curso
cards.translation: Future perfect emphasizes completion before a future deadline. ponerse con = start working on.

cards.front: By the time you arrive, I'll already have left
cards.front example: But I'll leave the keys for you.
cards.back: Cuando llegues, ya me habré ido
cards.translation: Me habré ido = future perfect of irse. When referring to the future, Spanish uses subjunctive after cuando.

cards.front: I would have finished earlier if I hadn't been interrupted
cards.front example: I lost almost an hour because of that.
cards.back: Habría terminado antes si no me hubieran interrumpido
cards.example: Perdí casi una hora con eso.
cards.translation: Conditional perfect + pluperfect subjunctive = unreal past condition and result.

cards.front: I would have accepted if the conditions had been different
cards.front example: But it wasn't worth it for me.
cards.back: Habría aceptado si las condiciones hubieran sido diferentes
cards.translation: Past hypothetical. compensar = to be worth it/pay off.

cards.front: What would you do in my situation?
cards.front example: I need an honest opinion.
cards.translation: Conditional is used for hypothetical questions and advice.

cards.front example: I want to know how you would have approached it.
cards.example: Quiero saber cómo lo habrías planteado.
cards.translation: Conditional perfect asks about an alternative past action. plantear = approach/frame a problem.

cards.front: I would never have imagined that
cards.front example: A few years ago, it would have seemed impossible to me.
cards.example: Hace unos años me habría parecido imposible.
cards.translation: Habría imaginado = unrealized past perspective. Useful for expressing surprise.

cards.front: A few years ago, I would have found this impossible
cards.front example: And now it's part of my everyday life.
cards.back: Hace unos años me habría parecido imposible
cards.example: Y ahora forma parte de mi día a día.
cards.translation: Habría parecido = conditional perfect for a hypothetical past perspective.

cards.front: I think I'll need to rethink my approach
cards.front example: Some things aren't working.
cards.back: Creo que tendré que replantearme el enfoque
cards.example: Hay cosas que no están funcionando.
cards.translation: Tendré que = I will have to. replantearse = reconsider/rethink; enfoque = approach.

cards.front: I'll probably end up changing my mind
cards.front example: The same thing always happens to me.
cards.translation: Acabar + gerund in future = will end up doing something.

cards.front example: But I wouldn't get my hopes up either.
cards.example: Pero tampoco me haría muchas ilusiones.
cards.translation: Descartar = rule out/discard. Conditional softens the statement.

cards.front: I wouldn't get my hopes up
cards.front example: Until we have something confirmed.
cards.translation: Hacerse ilusiones = get one's hopes up. Very natural emotional expression.

cards.front: That would make a huge difference
cards.front example: Especially in the long term.
cards.translation: Suponer = mean/represent/entail. Conditional is useful for hypothetical consequences.

cards.front example: If it really helps you make progress.
cards.example: Si realmente te ayuda a avanzar.
cards.translation: Merecer la pena = to be worth it. Conditional expresses hypothetical value.

cards.back: Colloquial expression used to strongly but casually say 'no' or deny something.
cards.translation: Very common in Spain. Means something like 'not at all'.

cards.back: Expression of surprise, disappointment, admiration, or reaction depending on tone.
cards.example: Vaya, no me esperaba esa noticia.
cards.translation: A very versatile Spanish reaction word.

cards.back: Used when a phrase fits perfectly in the context, often humorously.
cards.translation: Literally: 'never better said'.

cards.back: Expression used when something feels pleasant or satisfying.
cards.translation: Means something like 'it's a pleasure'.

cards.example: Hay muy buen rollo entre nosotros.
cards.translation: Opposite: mal rollo.

cards.example: Ese sitio me dio mal rollo.
cards.translation: Very common colloquial expression.

cards.back: Something involved or influencing the situation.
cards.example: Con buenas noticias de por medio, todo cambia.
cards.translation: Often used for emotions, problems, money, relationships, etc.

cards.back: To take a look at something.
cards.example: ¿Le puedes echar un ojo a estos resultados?
cards.translation: Very common informal expression.

cards.example: Después de todo el esfuerzo, te lo mereces.
cards.translation: Used for encouragement or recognition.

cards.back: Diminutive of 'momento'; sounds softer and affectionate.
cards.translation: Spanish often uses diminutives for emotional tone.

cards.back: Colloquial expression used to encourage, soften, or react.
cards.translation: Does not mean 'walk' in these contexts.

cards.back: Something surprised or shocked me strongly.
cards.example: La noticia me ha dejado loco.
cards.translation: Very colloquial.

cards.back: I understood you / I got what you mean.
cards.translation: Pillar often means 'to catch' or 'to get'.
Lío = mess, confusion.

cards.back: Friendly, informal tone; talking like friends.
cards.translation: Not a fixed expression, but natural.
Soft way to express disappointment.

cards.example: Ir de cervezas con amigos es un planazo.
cards.translation: -azo adds emphasis.

cards.example: Ya terminaste cinco capítulos, vas volando.
cards.translation: Literally: 'you're flying'.
From the verb tocar = to correspond/be the moment.

cards.back: Verb used for habits or things that usually happen.
cards.example: La gente suele tomar café por la mañana.
cards.translation: Structure: soler + infinitive.
Sonar often means 'to seem/sound'.
Not learning from zero.
Always used with 'en'.

cards.example: Estoy preparando una certificación de AWS.
cards.translation: The achievement/title.
The physical/digital proof.

cards.back: Meaning of a word or phrase.
cards.translation: Most common everyday word.

cards.example: La significación del símbolo es profunda.
cards.translation: Used in linguistics or formal analysis.
Very colloquial Spanish word.

cards.back: Present perfect continuous; emphasizes ongoing/recent process.
cards.example: He estado tomando pastillas estos meses.
cards.translation: Focuses on duration/process.

cards.back: Present perfect; focuses on completed action/result.
cards.translation: More neutral and factual.

cards.back: Example of imperfect subjunctive after pedir que.
cards.example: Le pedí que me diera una baja médica.
cards.translation: Structure: pedir que + subjuntivo.

cards.back: Past tense of recetar; used for doctors prescribing medicine.
cards.translation: Very common in medical contexts.

cards.back: To refer/send someone to a medical specialist.
cards.example: Quería saber si podían derivarme a cardiología.
cards.translation: Formal medical wording.
Medical vocabulary.

cards.example: Estoy en la sala de espera.
cards.translation: Common hospital vocabulary.
Medical vocabulary.
Very common emotional expression.
Very common greeting.
Used for reunions.

cards.back: A 'terapeuta' is a therapist or psychologist. 'Trapista' sounds like a Trappist monk.
cards.example: Tuve una sesión con mi terapeuta.
cards.translation: Similar words: psicólogo, terapeuta.

cards.back: Expression meaning 'I deserve it'. Uses reflexive verb merecerse.
cards.example: Después de esta semana, me lo merezco.
cards.translation: Related: te lo mereces, se lo merece.

cards.back: To tidy or organize the house.
cards.example: Hoy me toca ordenar un poco la casa.
cards.translation: Similar: limpiar la casa, recoger.

cards.back: Expression used when a doctor grants medical leave.
cards.example: La médica me dio una baja médica.
cards.translation: Related: estar de baja, coger una baja.

cards.back: To use an opportunity or free time for something useful.
cards.example: Estoy aprovechando esta semana para estudiar.
cards.translation: Similar: sacar provecho, utilizar el tiempo.

cards.back: To contact someone after a while or show that you are still around.
cards.translation: Related: aparecer otra vez, volver a escribir.

cards.back: Colloquial metaphor meaning mental chaos or too many thoughts mixed together.
cards.example: Tengo la cabeza en modo batidora.
cards.translation: Similar: caos mental, cabeza saturada.

cards.back: To mentally reorganize yourself or calm your thoughts.
cards.example: Necesitaba unos días para reordenar la cabeza.
cards.translation: Related: despejarse, aclarar las ideas.

cards.back: To clear one's mind or relax mentally.
cards.example: Salir a caminar me ayuda a despejarme.
cards.translation: Similar: relajarse, desconectar.

cards.back: To mentally disconnect from stress or work.
cards.example: Necesito desconectar este fin de semana.
cards.translation: Related: relajarse, tomarse un respiro.

cards.back: To take a break and breathe mentally/emotionally.
cards.example: Después de tanto estrés, necesito tomarme un respiro.
cards.translation: Similar: descansar un poco, desconectar.

cards.back: To get to the point directly.
cards.translation: Related: ser directo, no dar vueltas.

cards.back: To overcomplicate or avoid getting directly to the point.
cards.translation: Related: sobrepensar, complicarse.
Similar: entender, captar.

cards.back: To grasp or understand an idea.
cards.example: No capté la broma al principio.
cards.translation: Related: pillar, entender.

cards.example: He estado muy liado estos días.
cards.translation: Similar: ocupado, saturado.
Related: agobiado, sobrecargado.
Similar: saturado, estresado.

cards.example: Hoy me toca currar todo el día.
cards.translation: Formal version: trabajar.
Opposite: plan movido, fiesta.

cards.back: To go out for a drink or snack socially.
cards.translation: Related: ir de cañas, tomar una cerveza.
Related: tomar algo, ir a tomar una cerveza.

cards.back: Expression for being happy/excited about something.
cards.example: Me hace ilusión verte otra vez.
cards.translation: Similar: me alegra, me entusiasma.

cards.back: To like someone / someone gives a good impression.
cards.example: Tu amigo me cae muy bien.
cards.translation: Opposite: caer mal.

cards.back: To dislike someone / someone gives a bad impression.
cards.translation: Opposite: caer bien.

cards.back: Joking way to say you're busy or focused on something important.
cards.example: He estado desaparecido, estaba de misión.
cards.translation: Related: modo misión, ocupado.

cards.back: Focused state where someone is fully dedicated to a goal.
cards.example: Esta semana estoy en modo misión con AWS.
cards.translation: Similar: modo concentración, full focus.

cards.example: Eso suena a una muy buena idea.
cards.translation: Related: parece, da la impresión.
Similar: tener cuidado, ir con ojo.

cards.example: Ve con ojo con ese contrato.
cards.translation: Related: tener cuidado, estar atento.

cards.back: Literal meaning: the communion wafer in Catholicism. Real usage: a very common exclamation for surprise, shock, admiration, anger, etc.
cards.translation: Very Spanish. Tone completely changes meaning.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to fuck/have sex (vulgar). Real usage: used constantly as 'damn', 'fuck', 'seriously', etc.
cards.translation: One of the most common emotional words in Spain.

cards.back: Literal meaning: how strong. Real usage: something shocking, intense, unbelievable or emotionally impactful.
cards.translation: Very common reaction phrase.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to hallucinate/trip. Real usage: to be amazed, shocked or blown away.
cards.translation: Originally linked to drug culture decades ago.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to scratch/make lines. Real usage: to overthink, obsess or mentally spiral.
cards.example: No te rayes tanto por eso.
cards.translation: Mental stress vocabulary in Spain.

cards.back: Literal meaning: not even joking. Real usage: absolutely no way.
cards.translation: Strong informal refusal.

cards.back: Literal meaning: of prostitute mother. Real usage: amazing, excellent, fantastic.
cards.example: La cena estuvo de puta madre.
cards.translation: Very vulgar literally, but extremely common positively.

cards.back: Literal meaning: vagina/cunt (vulgar). Real usage: emotional exclamation similar to 'damn', 'come on', 'shit'.
cards.translation: Very contextual. Friends use it constantly.

cards.back: Literal meaning: go/walk already. Real usage: no way, come on, I don't believe you.
cards.translation: Can be playful disbelief.

cards.back: Literal meaning: my mother. Real usage: expression of surprise, stress, admiration or exhaustion.
cards.translation: Safe and universal expression.

cards.back: Literal meaning: fabric/cloth. Real usage: something intense, excessive or difficult.
cards.translation: Spain-specific metaphorical use.

cards.back: Literal meaning: it has fabric. Real usage: this situation is crazy/complicated/ridiculous.
cards.translation: Usually judgmental or dramatic.

cards.back: Literal meaning: in plan/in style. Real usage: filler word like English 'like'.
cards.example: Y yo en plan: ¿qué está pasando?
cards.translation: Young people use it nonstop.

cards.back: Literal meaning: now you see. Real usage: exactly, that's life, totally.
cards.translation: Agreement/resignation expression.

cards.back: Literal meaning: such which/exactly as. Real usage: exactly, literally true.
cards.translation: Very common modern phrase.

cards.back: Literal meaning: what a bastard/goat-like man. Real usage: can mean asshole OR lucky/funny bastard among friends.
cards.example: Te dieron vacaciones extra, qué cabrón.
cards.translation: Dangerous phrase if tone is wrong.

cards.back: Literal meaning: mallet/hammer. Real usage: very/a lot.
cards.translation: Classic Madrid slang.

cards.back: Literal meaning: uncle. Real usage: dude/guy/man.
cards.translation: Probably the most common social word in Spain.

cards.back: Literal meaning: tree trunk. Real usage: dude/bro.
cards.translation: Very Madrid/street style.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to work it for oneself. Real usage: to put effort into something.
cards.translation: Implies respect for effort.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to be up to the eggs/testicles. Real usage: to be fed up.
cards.example: Estoy hasta los huevos del estrés.
cards.translation: Extremely common vulgar phrase.

cards.back: Literal meaning: with big balls/testicle-related fear. Real usage: terrified or very nervous.
cards.translation: Very colloquial emotional word.

cards.back: Literal meaning: testicle-related. Real usage: excellent, awesome.
cards.translation: Funny positive vulgarity.

cards.back: Literal meaning: the communion wafer. Real usage: incredible, intense, crazy good/bad.
cards.translation: Can express admiration or intensity.

cards.back: Literal meaning: I shit on... Real usage: strong frustration expression.
cards.example: Me cago en todo, perdí el móvil.
cards.translation: Very Spanish swearing structure.

cards.back: Literal meaning: I pass. Real usage: I don't want to bother / I'm not interested.
cards.translation: Short casual refusal.

cards.back: Literal meaning: no literal modern meaning. Real usage: to be cool.
cards.translation: Essential colloquial Spain verb.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to explode/break something. Real usage: to crush it, become hugely successful.
cards.translation: Popular modern slang.

cards.back: Literal meaning: exploded/burst. Real usage: crowded, packed or exhausted.
cards.translation: Depends heavily on context.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to be made into dust. Real usage: physically or emotionally exhausted.
cards.translation: Very visual metaphor.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to assemble/set it up well for oneself. Real usage: to enjoy life/have a great time.
cards.example: Se lo montan bien los fines de semana.
cards.translation: Can imply partying or simply enjoying life.

cards.back: Literal meaning: what a passing. Real usage: amazing, incredible.
cards.translation: Strong positive admiration.

cards.back: Literal meaning: what a movement. Real usage: what a mess/drama/problem.
cards.example: Lo del trabajo es una movida.
cards.translation: Movida is deeply tied to Spanish slang culture.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to go for small beers. Real usage: casual social drinking/tapas culture.
cards.translation: Very Spanish social ritual.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to take something. Real usage: to go out socially for drinks/snacks.
cards.translation: Extremely common invitation.

cards.back: Literal meaning: slang work/job. Real usage: work, job, workload.
cards.translation: Informal everyday word.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to suffocate/oppress oneself. Real usage: to feel mentally overwhelmed.
cards.translation: Very emotionally expressive verb.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to catch/grab. Real usage: to understand/get.
cards.translation: Very versatile colloquial verb.

cards.back: Literal meaning: it already touched/it was its turn. Real usage: it was about time.
cards.translation: From tocar = one's turn/correspond.

cards.back: Literal meaning: it gives pleasure. Real usage: something feels pleasant/satisfying.
cards.translation: Warm positive expression.

cards.back: Literal meaning: good roll/vibe. Real usage: good atmosphere, positive energy.
cards.translation: One of the most useful social expressions.

cards.back: Literal meaning: bad roll/vibe. Real usage: tension, creepy or uncomfortable atmosphere.
cards.example: Ese sitio me da mal rollo.
cards.translation: Can describe people, places or situations.

cards.back: Literal meaning: no clear literal meaning. Real usage: cool, nice.
cards.translation: Classic Spain Spanish.

cards.back: Literal meaning: it cools me/pleases me (historically unclear). Real usage: I like it, it's cool.
cards.translation: Very colloquial positive opinion.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to hallucinate hard. Real usage: to be shocked/amazed.
cards.example: La vas a flipar cuando lo veas.
cards.translation: Very expressive modern slang.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to be in a downward state. Real usage: to feel emotionally low.
cards.example: Hoy estoy un poco de bajón.
cards.translation: Soft emotional expression.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to put batteries into oneself. Real usage: to get motivated/start acting seriously.
cards.example: Tengo que ponerme las pilas con el inglés.
cards.translation: Very visual and common phrase.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to go to the sack/bag. Real usage: to go all in/full force.
cards.example: Esta semana estoy yendo a saco con AWS.
cards.translation: Strong energy/focus expression.

cards.back: Literal meaning: to be at the parrot. Real usage: to pay attention/stay alert.
cards.example: Estate al loro con ese correo.
cards.translation: Funny old-school Spain expression.
